author: massicomar
title: Convex Hull
summary:
Given a set of $n$ points in the two-dimensional plane, your task is to determine the smallest convex poligon enclosing all of the points.

Input

The first input line has an integer $n$: the number of points.

After this, there are $n$ lines that describe the points. Each line has two integers $x$ and $y$: the coordinates of a point.

You may assume that each point is distinct, and the area of the hull is positive.

Output

First print an integer $k$: the number of points in the convex hull.

After this, print $k$ lines that describe the points. You can print the points in any order. Print all points that lie on the polygon.
explanation: Monotone chain, but this judge wants collinear boundary points kept: pop only on a strict right turn.
traps: The collinear rule is the opposite of Kattis Convex Hull.
